item.title: JavaScript, TypeScript & React Core Concepts
item.author: ThanhLD
item.description: JavaScript Fundamentals Closures A closure in JavaScript allows the function to remember the variables from the enclosing function where it was created, enabling encapsulation and state retention. Hoisting Hoisting in JavaScript is a behavior where variable and function declarations are moved to the top of their containing scope during the compile phase, before the code is executed. This means that you can use variables and functions before they are declared in the code.

item.title: Golang Deep Dive: Concurrency, Runtime & Architecture
item.author: ThanhLD
item.description: Concurrency & Channels Channel Types unbuffered channel An unbuffered channel does not have any capacity to store values. It requires both a sender and a receiver to be ready at the same time to complete the communication. A send operation will block until another goroutine is ready to receive, and vice versa. For example, I have a long-running task on the database. Running multiple tasks at once can cause an overload, so I can use a buffered channel to ensure that only one task can run at a time buffer channel A buffered channel has a capacity that allows it to store a specified number of values.

item.title: Microservices Architecture & Distributed System Design Patterns
item.author: ThanhLD
item.description: Monolith vs Microservices Architecture Monolithic Architecture Pros: - Simpler to develop and deploy: Single codebase, fewer moving parts. - Easier testing: End-to-end tests are straightforward. - Lower operational overhead: One unit to manage and deploy. Cons: Limited scalability: Scaling requires scaling the entire app. - Harder to maintain: As the app grows, managing the codebase becomes difficult. - Tight coupling: Changes in one part can affect the entire system. Microservices Architecture Pros: - Independent scalability: Scale each service based on need.

item.title: Database & Message Brokers: SQL, NoSQL & Queues
item.author: ThanhLD
item.description: Comprehensive notes on Relational Databases (SQL), In-Memory Caching (Redis), and Distributed Message Brokers (Kafka & RabbitMQ) for technical interviews and system architecture design. Relational Databases (SQL) SQL vs NoSQL ACID Properties in Relational Databases Atomicity: All operations in a transaction succeed or fail together. If any operation fails, the entire transaction is rolled back. (e.g. transfer money from Account A to Account B). Consistency: Any transaction brings the database from one valid state to another, strictly obeying all schema rules, constraints, triggers, and cascades.
